question.problem: Given that $X∼\text{Bernoulli}(0.5)$ and $Y∼\text{Bernoulli}(0.3)$ are independent, calculate $P(X=0\,\cap \,Y=0).$
question.worked_solution:
Using the multiplication law for independent events, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=0\,\cap \,Y=0) & =P(X=0)\cdot P(Y=0).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $X∼\text{Bernoulli}(0.5),$ we have

$$
P(X=1)=0.5,\,P(X=0)=0.5,
$$

and since $Y∼\text{Bernoulli}(0.3),$ we have

$$
P(Y=1)=0.3,\,P(Y=0)=0.7.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=0\,\cap \,Y=0) & =P(X=0)\cdot P(Y=0) \\  & =0.5\cdot 0.7 \\  & =0.35.\end{aligned}
$$
